bugs.title: audit.md YAML frontmatter silently dropped at runtime
bugs.description: audit.md's frontmatter description contained ': ' unquoted, so YAML parsing failed and Claude Code loaded the command with EMPTY metadata — description, argument-hint and allowed-tools never applied, since v0.2.0. init.md's argument-hint parsed as a YAML array instead of a string.
repro: claude plugin validate plugins/audit
observe: 'YAML frontmatter failed to parse ... loads with empty metadata'
bugs.expected: All four commands load with their declared metadata.
bugs.actual: audit.md loaded with empty metadata; init.md argument-hint was an array.
bugs.notes: Found by adopting claude plugin validate as a release gate; the gate is now enforced in CI.

bugs.title: journal_dir returns mixed path separators; j12 red on Windows
bugs.reportedBy: CI run 31427419994 (first Windows leg over the v0.29+ backlog)
bugs.description: scripts/audit-journal.py journal_dir() joins the project root with config-derived forward-slash components (os.path.dirname of manifestPath), returning e.g. C:\tmp\x\docs/audit\journal on Windows. hooks/_config.py j12 compares str(Path(answer)) == answer, which fails on the separator spelling alone. Same path, two spellings; also yields proj/./journal on POSIX when the manifest sits at the project root.
repro: python plugins/audit/hooks/_config.py --selftest  (on Windows: FAIL j12, 80/81)
bugs.expected: journal_dir returns one normalized spelling on every platform.
bugs.actual: Mixed separators on Windows; a redundant ./ segment on POSIX with a root manifest.
bugs.notes: Both returns normalise, so one spelling reaches every reader and the climbing segment a root-level manifest used to produce is gone.

bugs.title: panel policy view exceeds the 1560px capture viewport on Linux
bugs.description: capture-screenshots.mjs --check: the policy view renders 1590px tall in a 1560px viewport on ubuntu (Linux font metrics run taller than macOS), so the sticky save bar would cover table rows in a capture. The check's own comment prescribes the fix: raise the viewport.
repro: node tools/capture-screenshots.mjs --check  (on ubuntu: FAIL the policy view is 1590px tall...)
bugs.expected: The policy view fits the capture viewport on every CI platform.
bugs.actual: 1590px > 1560px on ubuntu; passes on macOS.
bugs.notes: The capture viewport is taller than the height the policy view was measured at, so no row sits behind the save bar in a shot.

bugs.title: ui/ assets CRLF-converted on Windows checkout; cross-line pins fail
bugs.reportedBy: CI run 31428171362 (Windows leg, after BF1 fixed j12)
bugs.description: scripts/ui/* are byte-precise build inputs read with newline='' (deliberate: the assembled UI_HTML/_CSS/_SCRIPT byte-identity depends on exact bytes). With no .gitattributes, windows-latest checkout (autocrlf) rewrites them to CRLF, so every selftest pin that spans a line boundary fails (panel-server: 'four sections are ONE list', 'wide data table scrolls'; render-report would fail the same way - the sweep stops at the first red).
repro: fresh checkout with core.autocrlf=true; python plugins/audit/scripts/panel/panel-server.py --selftest
bugs.expected: Assets reach every platform LF, and a CRLF asset is named by a selftest, not discovered via a distant pin.
bugs.actual: CRLF assets on Windows; two cross-line pins red; the real cause two files away from the failure.
bugs.notes: The byte-precise build inputs are declared to git, so a checkout that rewrites line endings cannot change what the assembled surfaces hash to.

bugs.title: sub-cent cost rule proven one module away from where it renders
bugs.reportedBy: P13.3 mutation pass (recorded as F10 in the private fault ledger)
bugs.description: Corrupting _report_usage's fmt_cost delegation and rerunning its own selftest stayed green - no fixture in that suite spends under a cent, so the <$0.01 rule is exercised only in _fmt's goldens. The consumer could stop delegating (or mangle the arguments) and its 49 cases would not notice; the parallel fmt_tokens mutation goes red in three cases by name, which is what the cost side should look like.
repro: weaken _fmt.fmt_cost delegation in _report_usage; python3 plugins/audit/scripts/report/_report_usage.py --selftest stays green
bugs.expected: A sub-cent spend asserted through the rendered tile string in _report_usage's own suite.
bugs.actual: Delegation-coverage gap; the rule is proven only where it is defined, not where it renders.
bugs.notes: The consumer's own suite now spends under a cent, so a delegation that stopped delegating would be caught there rather than only next door.

bugs.title: panel: a task's detail row renders away from the row it was opened on
bugs.reportedBy: the maintainer, reading the panel after v2.0.1
bugs.description: Opening a task in the panel draws its information row somewhere other than under the row that was opened - reported as rendering at the bottom. NOT YET REPRODUCED, and that is recorded rather than assumed: overview.js appends the data-evdetail row immediately after its own data-ovtask row, and evRollCells returns plain spans rather than toggles, so neither the append order nor a shared OVF.evOpen key explains it. Either the surface is the Composition tab instead, or the cause is CSS or re-render order. Reproduce in a browser before changing any code. REPRODUCTION ATTEMPT 2026-09-06, driven in a real browser against a generated demo project (3 phases, 4 tasks, evidence present): NOT REPRODUCED, and both hypotheses the report itself offered are refuted. (1) Overview tab, one task opened: the data-evdetail row lands at index taskRow+1, exactly one detail row open, no page errors. (2) Composition tab cannot be the surface - it renders ZERO [data-evtog] elements, so there is nothing there to open. (3) Two tasks opened at once: each detail row sits under its own task row, so no shared key moves the first. What remains untested is a real repository's data rather than the generator's, and a viewport narrow enough to change wrapping. Closing this needs the reporter's word, not this evidence alone.
repro: open the panel, expand a phase, open a task's detail, and read where the detail row lands relative to the row that was pressed
bugs.expected: the detail row is the next sibling of the row it belongs to.
bugs.actual: reported as rendering at the bottom, away from its own row.
bugs.notes: NOT REPRODUCIBLE on this build, 2026-09-06. Four hypotheses tested by driving a real browser, all refuted: (1) Overview, one task open - the detail row is at taskRow+1; (2) the Composition tab cannot be the surface, it renders zero [data-evtog]; (3) two tasks open at once - each detail row under its own task row; (4) mobile/tablet/wide viewports - the row PAINTS directly below its own, 0px gap, no console errors anywhere. Closed as not-reproducible rather than fixed: nothing was changed, so a fresh sighting with the conditions reopens it and this note says what has already been ruled out.

bugs.title: doctor's warn line calls a phase in_progress that only awaits sign-off even when its stored status is pending
bugs.description: manifest_state names the FIRST phase whose every task is terminal with no verdict recorded, whatever its stored status, and _doctor_setup's warn line then says that phase 'is in_progress but only awaits sign-off'. On this repo it named P32, stored pending.
repro: python3 plugins/audit/scripts/status/audit-doctor.py on this repo
read the plan gate line
bugs.expected: the line says only what is true of the phase it names, and names an in_progress one when there is one
bugs.actual: warn - no phase has work in flight: phase P32 is in_progress but only awaits sign-off ... (P32 is pending)

bugs.title: close-phase judges cleanup by the phase as it stood BEFORE its own merge, so a phase signed off on its branch is refused cleanup as 'pending'
bugs.description: Run from the parent worktree (the only place a worktree phase can land from), close-phase loads the parent's manifest, where the sign-off - committed on the phase branch - is not yet present. It merges, stamps mergedAt into the merged copy, and then judges the worktree and branch cleanup with settlement(phase, merged=True) on the PRE-merge phase dict, which reads 'pending'. The refusal says sign-off has not passed, which is false, and a second run is needed.
repro: sign off a phase in its linked worktree
from the parent worktree: close-phase.py <plan> <phase> --project .
bugs.expected: the merge lands and the cleanup is judged against the phase as the merge left it: signed off and merged, so the worktree and branch are removed
bugs.actual: not done: phase P64 is 'pending', not 'done' - sign-off has not passed (P64 was signed off; the merge had just brought that in)
bugs.notes: found landing P64, 2026-09-24. The second run it forces, 'already-contained', also re-stamps mergedAt with its own time (21:43:52 became 21:44:12), so the record stops naming the moment of the merge.

bugs.title: journal-writes derives completion rows from a git merge's write, recording a second task.complete for work the merged branch already records
bugs.description: The hook's sweep lane compares each recorded path's digest before and after a Bash call. A `git merge` of a phase branch moves the manifest and the phase shard, so the pass diffs them and emits manifest.edit plus task.complete / task.commit rows for every task the branch finished - rows the branch's own journal already carries. Landing P65 wrote task.complete and task.commit for P65.1 a second time, into the conflicted journal file; the completion count the doctor reads is no longer a count of completions.
repro: finish a task on a phase branch
from the parent tree: git merge <branch> in a Bash call
audit-journal.py show: a second task.complete for that task
bugs.expected: a write that brings in another branch's recorded history derives no completion rows - those completions happened, and were recorded, where the work ran
bugs.actual: task.complete P65.1 and task.commit P65.1 appended again by the hook after the merge

bugs.title: commit-manifest-index commits an index whose fileIndex names tasks their phase's shard has not committed, so the commit records a plan that does not validate
bugs.description: audit-task add writes the new task into the phase shard and its files into the index's fileIndex. commit-manifest-index then commits the index alone - by design, so no phase's work rides with it - while the shard stays uncommitted until commit-audit-state. Every commit in between records an index naming tasks no committed shard holds, and verify-invariants' manifest-revalidated reports each as a breach. Measured on P66: three task commits in breach because commit-audit-state was not run after each task; nothing refused or warned when the index went ahead of its shard.
repro: audit-task add <task> --phase <phase> on a sharded plan
commit-manifest-index <plan> <phase>
git show HEAD:<index> plus HEAD's shard: validate-manifest reports fileIndex naming a task that does not exist
bugs.expected: the index is committed only in a state the committed shards support - or commit-manifest-index says which shard must be committed with it, and does not leave a commit that fails validation
bugs.actual: the index commit lands; the plan as that commit records it fails validation until the shard is committed later

bugs.title: manage-worktrees list/remove/sweep compose a phase's branch without the git user's initials, so the worktree add just cut is a stranger to its own tool
bugs.description: Since start performs phase entry, manage-worktrees add names the branch through _branch.phase_answer(meta, phase, git user name), which applies a meta.branch template's initials. list, remove, sweep and parents_of still compose it through wanted_branches(manifest) / parents_of(manifest) with no user name. Under a template with initials the two disagree: the worktree add created is listed as a stranger and remove says no worktree holds the phase's branch. Unreleased regression; 3.0.1 composed the wrong name in both places and so agreed with itself. This repo's own template has no initials, which is why dogfooding cannot see it.
repro: a plan whose meta.branch template carries the user's initials (resolve-branch.py --phase P48 prints feature/ab/p48-...)
manage-worktrees.py add <plan> P48 -> branch feature/ab/p48-...
manage-worktrees.py list <plan> -> owned=[] strangers=[feature/ab/p48-...] missing=[feature/p48-...]
manage-worktrees.py remove <plan> P48 -> exit 1, no worktree holds feature/p48-...
bugs.expected: every manage-worktrees verb names a phase's branch the way add and resolve-branch do, so add then list shows the worktree as owned and remove finds it
bugs.actual: add cuts feature/ab/p48-...; list, remove and sweep look for feature/p48-...

repro: Apply p83-handoff/p83.5-red-tests.patch on main after P83 lands
python3 plugins/audit/tests/test_guard_history_rewrite.py --selftest
python3 plugins/audit/tests/test__config.py --selftest

bugs.title: the history guard allows a rewrite when the cd target's path contains a space
bugs.description: Measured by the P94.4 probe (it calls only the guard's own readers): _config.effective_cwd dropped a quoted cd into a directory whose name contained a space (it answered None for cd '<dir with a space>' && git rebase main), so the history guard judged the call against the payload's working directory instead of the worktree the shell moved into. A rebase or reset of a worktree's recorded commit was therefore allowed whenever the cd target's path contained a space - an ordinary path on macOS and Windows. test_guard_history_rewrite gw2 now creates its worktree under such a path and denies the correctly quoted reset.
bugs.notes: Fixed by the human maintainer on branch fix/bug-13 (5adb3bba, 3744a6b4, 9ea779f1): a cd target whose name holds a space, quoted or backslash-escaped, is followed, and gw2/gw2b pin it. Reviewed twice until clean and landed through P95 (task P95.1). The wider fallback when a cd or -C value cannot be placed at all is BUG-14; the review's low edges are PLAN.md F547.

bugs.title: the guards judge a command where the shell does not run it when a cd or -C target cannot be placed
bugs.description:
When _config.effective_cwd cannot place a cd, pushd or -C target, it returns None, and its callers then judge the command somewhere other than where the shell runs it. This covers a target held in a variable, a home shorthand, `cd -`, a bare cd, popd, an unbalanced quote and a -C value it cannot read. The spaced-path half of this was BUG-13, fixed in P95; this bug is the unplaceable half. Each caller was measured through its own function, benign reads only.
- History guard: after an unreadable cd, the call is judged against the session's directory. An unreadable -C value is judged against the project from any session. Either way, a rewrite of a worktree's recorded commit is allowed (test_guard_history_rewrite gw12 and gw13 are red on main).
- Release guard (.claude/hooks/guard-release.py, resolved_tree): after an unreadable cd, it falls back to the session's directory. It also does not read a -C value at all, so `git -C <worktree>` from a project session is judged against the project.
- journal-writes: rows are placed in the session's directory after an unreadable cd.
- guard-secrets-read: does not fall back. A relative write target after an unreadable cd is reported as unestablished, which is the intended shape.
The repair direction: a guard that cannot place the command answers ask or deny, never the session's directory. Part 2 of the BUG-13 handoff has the red cases (gw12, gw13). A red case is still owed for guard-release: an unreadable cd into a worktree with an open bug must be refused, and a resolvable cd into a clean tree is its allow twin. This is the guards' reading code, so the fix is the human maintainer's.
bugs.notes: Fixed by the human maintainer on branch fix/bug-14 (ff194c30, aad1aa87, 536f017a, e3afc4ae, bbc0be38): a cd/pushd/popd/-C target this cannot place, and a payload naming no cwd at all, both answer unplaceable now instead of falling back to the session or project; gw12-gw15 and gw14b-gw14h pin it, and guard-release's own selftest covers the release guard's half. Reviewed four times until clean and landed through P97 (task P97.1). A heredoc-blind asymmetry in guard-release's own _shell_moves, found during the fourth review, is BUG-15 - a different, pre-existing defect in a different file, filed separately rather than folded into this one.

bugs.title: guard-release's _shell_moves reads a heredoc body as live text, so a payload with no cwd over-refuses
bugs.description: A PreToolUse payload naming no cwd falls to _session_base, which asks _shell_moves(cfg_mod, command) whether the command moves the shell at all. That function is fed the RAW command text, unlike guard-history-rewrite.py own _shell_moves, which is fed runnable(command) - the same text with a heredoc body destined for a file already stripped, as every reading in that file does. A heredoc body that is pure file data and happens to contain a line starting with cd is read by guard-release.py as a real directory change, so a payload with no cwd and such a command is answered unplaceable (refused as UNKNOWN by callers that gate a publishing release on it) even though the shell never moves. Found while reviewing the BUG-14 fix e3afc4ae on fix/bug-14: pre-existing on main, not introduced by that commit - the asymmetry surfaced only because guard-history-rewrite.py was given the correct, heredoc-aware behaviour as part of that fix.
bugs.repro: call _shell_moves(cfg_mod, command) directly (or decide(command, project, session_id, payload={"tool_input": {"command": command}}) with no payload cwd key) on a command built as the heredoc `cat > deploy.txt <<'EOF'`, a line reading `cd /somewhere`, a line reading the git publish verb with the force flag, then the `EOF` terminator - a heredoc body whose text happens to contain a cd line
bugs.expected: False - the heredoc body is file data; the shell never runs a cd, so a payload with no cwd should answer to the project the same way guard-history-rewrite.py own _shell_moves already does on the identical command
bugs.actual: True - _shell_moves reads the raw command text, sees the literal "cd /somewhere" line inside the heredoc body, and judges it a real directory change
bugs.notes: Fixed by the human maintainer across seven rounds of fix-then-review on fix/bug-15 (7f8a9fd2..fc7210f6); landed via P99.1.

bugs.title: guard-release's _publishers matches a tag/push/release pattern inside ANY quoted text, heredoc or not
bugs.description: While researching BUG-15, found _publishers (and the _TAG_AT/_PUSH_AT/_GH_AT regexes it drives) tracks no quote state at all - it is a plain regex scan over the raw command string. Any text that merely LOOKS like a boundary-preceded publishing invocation is read as a real one, whether it sits inside a single-quoted string, a double-quoted string, or a heredoc body - no heredoc is required to trigger it, which makes this broader than BUG-15 and not fixed by the same runnable(command) swap. Confirmed live: a research command describing a release step in prose, quoted with single quotes, with double quotes, and separately placed inside a heredoc destined for a file and inside one destined for python3, were ALL read by _publishers as a real tag-creating invocation - in the heredoc-to-python3 case the describing text was a Python string literal, never shell at all. The live guard actually refused this very bug report while it was being filed, because the repro text itself matched the pattern it describes - confirming the class is already reachable by ordinary work, not only by a crafted exploit. Over-refusal direction (safe, not a fail-open), but it can block ordinary documentation or script-writing work whenever its content happens to describe a publishing step after a separator word.
bugs.repro: call _publishers(command) with command built from a plain echo of a release-step description, once in single quotes and once in double quotes, and separately from a heredoc (one destined for cat, one destined for python3) whose body contains that same description, where the description itself happens to read as a boundary-preceded publishing invocation
bugs.expected: no publishers detected in any of the four forms above - the description text never actually invokes a publishing command, it only appears inside something the current shell treats as inert (a quoted string, or a heredoc body)
bugs.actual: _publishers reports a publishing invocation in all four forms - its regex boundary match fires on the separator before the embedded text regardless of the quoting or heredoc context around it, with no tracking of whether that span is actually live shell text
bugs.notes: Fixed by the human maintainer across seven rounds of fix-then-review on fix/bug-15 (7f8a9fd2..fc7210f6); landed via P99.1.

bugs.title: audit-task start copies the index-only priority into the phase shard
bugs.description: On the sharded layout, starting a phase's first task writes the phase's priority into the shard body. priority is an index-only field, so the validator warns on every later run and the copy is ignored. The stub already carries it, so start should leave the shard without it.
bugs.repro: git archive main's docs/audit into a fresh git repo; on that copy the P100 index stub carries priority 1 and the P100 shard carries none; run audit-task.py start P100.1 docs/audit/audit-plan.json --project-dir <copy>; grep priority in docs/audit/phases/P100.json; run validate-manifest.py
bugs.expected: the shard stays without priority, and validate-manifest prints no priority warning
bugs.actual: start exits 0; the shard gains priority 1; validate-manifest warns that priority sits in the shard body where nothing reads it. Seen in this repo's P100 shard in commit 2ec163d7, and reproduced on 3.1.0 on 2026-10-06

bugs.title: the usage ledger counts a message's streaming partial, undercounting output tokens
bugs.description: usage_ledger keeps the first transcript entry per message id; a transcript can write a streaming partial (stop_reason null) before the final entry under the same id, so output tokens are undercounted. Found by the native-cost pilot on 2026-10-06; fixed by task P104.9-tog.
bugs.repro: a headless claude -p run that spawns one subagent; meter its transcript with meter-usage
bugs.expected: each message id counted once at its final entry; the ledger sum matches Claude Code's total_cost_usd when the price table is current
bugs.actual: the subagent's output was counted as 4 tokens against 289 final, and the ledger summed below the native total by exactly that shortfall

bugs.title: status's UNFINISHED line gives every locked phase the plan-wide ready count
bugs.description: The UNFINISHED section of /audit:status prints one line per held phase lock and says that phase has N tasks still ready. N is the ready list of the whole plan, not the phase's own count, so every locked phase shows the same number. A phase whose own tasks are all done therefore reads as having work left. Read on the development branch, the count also comes from that branch's copies of the phase shards. A phase whose work lives on its own branch is shown with tasks ready that are already done there, and the line does not say which copy it read. The maintainer read the line as remaining work in each phase.
bugs.repro: Hold phase locks for several phases while the plan has ready tasks in other phases, then run /audit:status: every UNFINISHED line names the same count.
bugs.expected: Each line counts the ready tasks of its own phase, read from the copy that holds that phase live, and says which copy it read; a phase with no ready task of its own gets no ready-work line.
bugs.actual: Each line prints len(ready) over the whole plan; main reads its own stale shard copy for phases whose work is on a branch.

bugs.title: status's ready list and phase table show in-flight phases from the development branch's stale copy
bugs.description: On the development branch, /audit:status's READY NOW list, its phase table and its progress counts read each in-flight phase from the development branch's own copy of the shard. A phase whose work is happening on its own branch, in a linked worktree, is therefore shown with tasks ready or pending that are already done there. The status does not say which copy it read. Only the UNFINISHED block reads the live copy. The maintainer read the stale ready list as work left to do.
bugs.repro: With a phase in flight in a linked worktree and some of its tasks done there, run /audit:status on the development branch: those tasks are listed as ready or pending.
bugs.expected: Every surface counts an in-flight phase from the copy that holds it live, through the same reader the UNFINISHED block uses, and says which copy it read.
bugs.actual: The ready list, table and counts read the development branch shard; only UNFINISHED reads the live copy.

bugs.title: a shell append to the audit journal passes every PreToolUse hook while Edit of the same journal is refused
bugs.description: echo '{}' >> docs/audit/journal/<file>.jsonl is allowed at observe, warn and deny (test_hooks.py row b10), while Edit of the same file (b09) is denied at every tier by guard-edits; today only journal-writes records the append and guard-bash-writes reports it after the fact. Decided 2026-10-06 that the shell append is deny: one operation gets one verdict, and the edit tools already refuse the journal. Fixing it removes b10's known-divergence mark in test_hooks.py.
bugs.repro: PreToolUse for Bash with command: echo '{}' >> docs/audit/journal/x.jsonl, in a project with an audit plan
bugs.expected: deny at every tier, as Edit of the journal is
bugs.actual: allow at every tier

bugs.title: guard-secrets-read refuses a program whose string literal only mentions opening a secret file
bugs.description: A python3 - <<'PY' program whose only reference is a string literal naming open('.env'), and which reads nothing, is denied at every tier with the heredoc secret-read refusal (test_hooks.py row g06): the guard matches the program's text, not an operation it performs. Decided 2026-10-06 that this is allow. Fixing it removes g06's known-divergence mark in test_hooks.py.
bugs.repro: PreToolUse for Bash with a python3 heredoc whose body is DOC = "the guard refuses open('.env') in a program"; print(len(DOC))
bugs.expected: allow: nothing is read
bugs.actual: deny at every tier

bugs.title: a redirect inside a subshell or command substitution is not seen as a shell write
bugs.description: guard-secrets-read's shell-write reader does not descend into subshell or command-substitution bodies. A redirect inside `( ... )` or `$( ... )` is therefore not seen as a write at all, at any tier: `(echo x > src/b.py)` and `x=$(echo x > src/b.py)` both answer ('allow', 'bash: no secret read') at deny, where the same `echo x > src/b.py` outside the parentheses is graded. A `{ ...; }` group is seen. Combined with an interpreter write in the same command, the interpreter's file takes the trivial slot and the subshell's file is written with no verdict. Observed at HEAD and in the P108.4 working tree (round-2 review, reproduced against a git-archive HEAD copy of the hooks).
bugs.repro: at the deny tier with an in_progress phase, a Bash command '(echo x > src/b.py)' or 'x=$(echo x > src/b.py)' where src/b.py is uncovered
bugs.expected: graded like 'echo x > src/b.py': the plan-gate verdict for an uncovered file
bugs.actual: allow, 'bash: no secret read'

bugs.title: free text written through audit-task reaches the hash-chained journal with a home-directory path in it
bugs.description: _journal_io's redaction section answers structural fields before row_hash() and leaves free prose to the after-the-fact detector in tools/check-committed-pii.py. For free text a verb takes from its caller (task notes, outcomes, reasons, finding text), the detector's verdict comes too late: the row is already hash-chained, and correcting it would break verify() on every clone, so the only remedy left is a BASELINE row that commits the leak permanently. Observed 2026-10-07: an executor's task note quoted a command with an absolute home path; the manifest copy was corrected by hand, but the journal row of the same note keeps the path and turned check-committed-pii's q7/q26/q27 red in the P108 worktree.
bugs.repro: audit-task.py note <taskId> --text 'Command: python3 /Users/<name>/project/x.py' in a project whose journal is on
bugs.expected: the write is refused (or the path reduced to a structural token) before the row is hashed, naming the field and the path shape, so a machine path never becomes a permanent row
bugs.actual: the row is hashed and written with the path; tools/check-committed-pii.py reports posix-home only afterwards, when the chain already runs through the row and it can only be baselined, never corrected

deferred.note: Consciously cut; each has a revisit trigger.

items.title: dry-run / preview mode
items.reason: status + the ready-list (and P3.3 report) already answer 'what would run'; a true no-side-effect executor doubles orchestrator complexity.

items.title: plugin-shipped agents/ (audit-explorer/executor/reviewer)
items.reason: genuinely promising (pinned tools/models per subagent) but a flagship on its own; shipping it half-baked next to ADO sync violates '3 excellent > 7 mediocre'.

items.title: Agent-Teams events integration (TaskCreated/TaskCompleted/TeammateIdle)
items.reason: build ON the native events once the surface stabilizes, not against it while experimental.

items.title: PostToolUse Bash diff-check (full shell-write coverage)
items.reason: the complete control for the statically-undecidable write vectors documented in SECURITY.md; costed, waiting for field demand.

items.title: a per-worktree browser capture, so the shots gate stops serialising parallel task runs
items.reason: the 'shots' entry (node tools/capture-screenshots.mjs --check) claims a FIXED per-user scratch tree under a lockfile and refuses outright while another capture holds it -- claimScratch(), which --check reaches too -- so every task gate carrying that entry is machine-wide exclusive: tasks run in parallel worktrees queue or fail there rather than in their own trees, and the failure names another run's pid. It stays on the task gate rather than only at sign-off because it is the one check that proves the report and the panel still paint, and a page found broken at sign-off is found after the work that broke it was committed. So the cost is paid deliberately: run browser gates from the orchestrator, not from inside parallel agents. Revisit when the capture can claim a tree per worktree (its byte-comparability argument pins the path, so that is the work), or when a measured parallel run loses more wall clock to the lock than the re-work it prevents.

proposals.name: the plugin's value is measured, not asserted
proposals.benefit: one end-to-end pipeline run on a fixture shows what a task costs and delivers through the plugin's own commands, and a reproducible with/without comparison on a feature-sized task reports outcome, cost, time and interventions per arm

phase.title: the plugin's value is measured, not asserted
phase.description: Tasks: (1) Pilot: one paid /audit:run end to end on the benchmark fixture, hard cap 4.50 USD (--max-budget-usd), recording what the orchestrator prose drives, cost per stage and where it stalls; this unblocks the decision on moving prose rules into scripts. (2) Design a subscription-based comparison: one feature-sized task in a brownfield fixture repo with hidden acceptance tests; arms = plain Claude Code, Claude Code with the same skills and a short CLAUDE.md, and the plugin's pipeline; same model, pinned CLI version, same skills, fresh session per run, randomized order; measure acceptance tests, out-of-scope changes, false completion claims, human interventions, wall clock, tokens and list-price equivalent, and share of the subscription window; scenarios: feature, bugfix, interrupted session plus resume, a step a guard must stop. (3) Run it within an agreed subscription time budget, n>=2 per arm, and publish the result with its limits.
phase.desiredOutcome: one end-to-end pipeline run on a fixture shows what a task costs and delivers through the plugin's own commands, and a reproducible with/without comparison on a feature-sized task reports outcome, cost, time and interventions per arm

phase.title: red-first proves a red outside Python

(3) Every entry point's usage error names its own version and, through one shared hook, the newer installed copy for this project; orchestrator docs resolve the plugin root per spawn and re-resolve after an update.

(2) Phase status and claim are written by a verb, not a hand edit. (3) executor.runsGate is resolved by a script, not by the model reading config. proposals.name: state writes never lose each other
proposals.benefit: two plugin writers running at once never silently drop each other's write: close-phase stamps under the index lock with an atomic rollback, a stale journal lock is broken by exactly one waiter, usage backfill keeps rows appended during its window, and the import-layer lint refuses a state write outside the sanctioned writers

phase.title: state writes never lose each other
phase.description: Tasks: (1) close-phase stamp_merged and record_merged_head under the index lock close-phase already takes for the stub mirror, rollback through atomic_write_json. (2) The stale journal lock is claimed by rename so only one waiter breaks it (no false tamper verdict). (3) Backfill re-reads the month file's tail after its replace, with no lock on the Stop hook's hot path. (4) A _deps rule: os.replace on plan or ledger paths only through sanctioned writers; reduce or justify the existing sites. Mechanisms reproduced by fixtures; not observed in 100 dogfood phases, hence after the higher-value phases.
phase.desiredOutcome: two plugin writers running at once never silently drop each other's write: close-phase stamps under the index lock with an atomic rollback, a stale journal lock is broken by exactly one waiter, usage backfill keeps rows appended during its window, and the import-layer lint refuses a state write outside the sanctioned writers

proposals.name: every command and reference hands scripts no manifest placeholder
proposals.benefit: no command or reference document asks the model to fill in a manifest path a script can resolve, and the rule for where the manifest is lives in one resolver

phase.title: every command and reference hands scripts no manifest placeholder
phase.description:
The orchestrator-driven commands and reference documents still hand the model a <manifestPath> placeholder to fill in, and three of them hand it to a script that now resolves the manifest itself. Remaining sites, as recorded when the first-contact commands were fixed:
- commands/phase.md:110 (audit-status.py)
- commands/task.md:171 (audit-status.py)
- reference/orchestrator.md:92, 102 and 723 (audit-status.py)
- commands/status.md:346 (verify-invariants.py, which does not resolve)

The rule is also copied in two places: plugins/audit/scripts/manifest/audit-task.py:96-97 and :1479, and plugins/audit/scripts/panel/_panel_paths.py:139. Default-path constants exist in _journal_io.py:337, hooks/_config.py:153, _doctor_setup.py:773 and _doctor_trail.py:944.

Route every script a command or reference document hands a manifest through _manifest_io.resolve_manifest, drop the placeholders, and fold the copies of the rule into the one resolver where the layer rule allows. The acceptance includes one of two things: either manifest_placeholder_drift scans reference/ as well as commands/, or explicit pending rows cover orchestrator.md. MANIFEST_PLACEHOLDER_PENDING empties as each command is repaired.
phase.desiredOutcome: no command or reference document asks the model to fill in a manifest path a script can resolve, and the rule for where the manifest is lives in one resolver
